description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a quintessential Hong Kong bakery delight known for their distinctively crunchy, sugary crust and soft, fluffy bread underneath. Despite the name, there is no pineapple in the bun; the topping's criss-cross pattern and golden color resemble a pineapple's skin. Enjoy these warm from the oven for a truly authentic Chinese breakfast or snack experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine bread flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Add warm milk and the beaten egg, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Incorporate the softened butter and continue kneading for another 5-7 minutes until the dough is very smooth and passes the windowpane test.

instructions.title: First Proof
instructions.text: Place the kneaded dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it proof in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until it has doubled in size. This step is crucial for a soft bun texture.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is proofing, cream together softened butter and granulated sugar for the topping until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk. In a separate bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, baking powder, and milk powder (if using). Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, mixing until just combined and a soft dough forms. Wrap it in plastic and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns and Apply Topping
instructions.text: Punch down the risen dough and divide it into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Take the chilled topping dough and divide it into 8 equal portions. Flatten each topping portion into a disc large enough to cover the top of a bun. Gently place a topping disc over each dough ball, pressing lightly to adhere. You can score a criss-cross pattern on the topping with a knife for the classic pineapple look.

instructions.title: Second Proof
instructions.text: Arrange the prepared buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them proof in a warm place for another 45-60 minutes, or until visibly puffy and about 1.5 times their original size.

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly brush the topping of each bun with beaten egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy, and the buns are cooked through. The bottom of the buns should also be lightly golden.

tips: Achieving a perfect windowpane test for the dough ensures a soft, fluffy bun. If it tears easily, knead for a few more minutes.
The topping dough should be firm enough to handle but not crumbly. If it's too sticky, add a touch more flour; if too dry, a tiny bit of milk.
Ensure your oven is fully preheated before baking to get the best rise and a crisp topping. Avoid opening the oven door during the first 10 minutes of baking.
